children: Sterlite Technologies shares hit the upper circuit limit of 5 percent on Friday after the broadband technology company approved a Rs 3,000-crore capital expenditure plan to expand capacity at its existing manufacturing facility.
Shares of the company quoted at Rs 748.90 per share on the NSE, up 5 percent, hitting the highest permissible trading limit for the day.

The company said the proposed capacity addition will increase its existing installed manufacturing capacity by approximately 50 percent. The additional capacity is expected to be added by the end of FY29.
Sterlite Technologies said the expansion is being undertaken in view of demand for optical fibre cables and connectivity business globally.
The company's existing capacity utilisation is around 70 percent.
The stock had fallen 0.15 percent on Thursday. After the company issued the update after market hours, it recovered those losses on Friday.
Brokerage CLSA has an 'Outperform' rating on Sterlite Technologies with a target price of Rs 950, implying an upside potential of more than 33 percent from the previous day's closing level.
In takeaways from a virtual analyst meet, the brokerage said the management sees the business at a pivotal moment, with the scale of opportunity significantly enhanced by AI data centres.
AI data centres have needs that are different from traditional data centres, including higher AI density driving multi-fold growth, besides interconnection between data centres, the brokerage said.
In addition to the opportunity in US data centres, the Indian market will also see 10G by 2030 from the current 1.5GW, it said.
India's data centre market will provide an added opportunity for STL to extend its global relationships to the home market, according to the brokerage.
STL is targeting Rs 200 billion in revenue by FY29, compared with the brokerage's estimate of Rs 104 billion, with a margin of 27 percent against the estimate of 23 percent.

The company will expand capacity to 1.5 times to enable its next growth phase and will invest Rs 10 billion annually, including in a new greenfield manufacturing facility in India, the brokerage said.

title: Sterlite Tech shares hit upper circuit on Rs 3,000 capex announcement, brokerage sees 33% upside
